newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee gains on late sale of dollars.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee gains on late sale of dollars.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee regained lost ground when a bank began selling dollars, after the exchange rate reached the top of the central bank range, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.20 to the dollar, after recovering from a low of 57.31, they said. The currency opened at its previous closing level of 57.25.
"The rupee fell to 57.31 which was the Central Bank top, due to trade backed demand, but bounced back when a bank began selling dollars," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Anything over 57.20 was a good level at which to sell, with the upside capped at 57.31, he said.
The Central Bank buying and selling prices were 56.1825 and 57.3125.
Overnight call rates plunged to a low of 12.625 percent, with the market well offered.
"Low money rates also go towards the market being well supplied with dollars, because the cost of holding the currency is reasonable," said a Deutsche Bank dealer.
